tract-buckeye-tech-corridor-az.name: Buckeye Tech Corridor
tract-buckeye-tech-corridor-az.source: Tract plans 1,700-acre data center campus in Phoenix, Arizona
tract-buckeye-tech-corridor-az.notes: Master-planned data center park on a ~2,069-acre former residential (Cipriani) parcel Tract acquired for ~$136M, south of I-10 in Buckeye; planned for up to ~20M sq ft across as many as 40 data centers at full build-out over ~15 years (~$20B). Coordinates are an approximate town-level geocode (Buckeye, south of I-10), not a parcel-confirmed point.

calethos-lithium-valley-imperial-county-.name: CalEthos Lithium Valley Data Center Campus
calethos-lithium-valley-imperial-county-.source: CalEthos expands data center plans for Lithium Valley, California, with 315-acre land purchase
calethos-lithium-valley-imperial-county-.notes: First phase now ~300-420MW (expanded from an original 80-acre/300MW plan; a range, so omitted from capacityMw); part of a planned 1M sq ft, 3-4 phase campus. Land purchase completed; permitting/engineering underway with American Dark Fiber. Distinct, competing developer from the existing tracked Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing (Sebastian Rucci/IVCM) project in the same county. Coordinates are approximate.

beacon-golden-valley-ca.name: Golden Valley Technology Hub
beacon-golden-valley-ca.developer: Beacon Data Centers (w/ California Resources Corp)
beacon-golden-valley-ca.source: Canada's Beacon DC targets 275MW data center campus on California oil field
beacon-golden-valley-ca.notes: 400,000 sq ft on 100 acres, dedicated 275MW from CRC's own Elk Hills natural gas power plant, closed-loop cooling. Standalone campus on former oilfield, not a colo tenancy.

databank-vernon-la-ca.name: Vernon LA Campus (with Goodman Group)
databank-vernon-la-ca.source: DataBank and Goodman Group partner to open new landmark data center in Los Angeles
databank-vernon-la-ca.notes: Joint venture with Goodman Group; opening December 2026, phased through September 2027.

ryan-companies-project-swan-lakeland-fl.name: Project Swan
ryan-companies-project-swan-lakeland-fl.source: Hyperscale data center proposed for Lakeland
ryan-companies-project-swan-lakeland-fl.notes: 600,000 sq ft across 3 buildings on 60.5 acres (4 parcels, near 923 Wilkinson Rd). Zoning may prohibit the project — data centers are not in Lakeland's Land Development Code — and part of the site is unincorporated Polk County, requiring annexation.

t5-atlanta-iv-palmetto-ga.name: T5 @ Atlanta IV
t5-atlanta-iv-palmetto-ga.water_notes: Air and liquid cooling designed for high-density AI workloads.
t5-atlanta-iv-palmetto-ga.source: T5 files to develop data center campus outside Atlanta, Georgia
t5-atlanta-iv-palmetto-ga.notes: City discrepancy: the ledger cited Fairburn, but T5's own page and PR Newswire list Palmetto, GA; DCD describes it as Fairburn/Fulton County with a 91-acre site in Palmetto - site is on the Fairburn/Palmetto border in South Fulton County (I-85 and Gullatt Rd). Capacity: T5's page lists '200 MW available' (Phase 1) while the Aug 2024 land-acquisition PR cites '300 MW' campus total - 300 MW recorded as planned. No tenant disclosed (T5 is a wholesale/build-to-suit developer targeting hyperscalers; page cites AI/liquid-cooling suitability). Phase 1 construction targeted Q2 2027; on-site substation expected 2026. No investment or jobs figure disclosed. Coordinates approximate (I-85/Gullatt Rd corridor).

microsoft-ginger-west-ia.name: Microsoft Project Ginger West Data Center
microsoft-ginger-west-ia.location: West Des Moines, Polk County, IA
microsoft-ginger-west-ia.water_notes: Microsoft's West Des Moines datacenters use direct evaporative cooling (water ~10% of the year, air-cooled the rest); a planned Ginger West building is committed to next-generation 'zero-water' cooling under WDM's 2023 policy favoring reduced peak water use. Microsoft's WDM fleet (five campuses) used ~70M gallons in 2024 (fleet-wide, not Ginger West-specific); Microsoft funded ~$25M in WDM Water Works improvements incl. a 2M-gallon tank.
microsoft-ginger-west-ia.source: Ginger West datacenter construction update — Microsoft Local
microsoft-ginger-west-ia.notes: Site at 11100 Booneville Rd area, West Des Moines (Polk County). 1.8M sq ft planned across multiple buildings. Turner Construction is general contractor; completion estimated summer 2028. Companion Ginger East campus (124 acres, 5 buildings) is a separate site in West Des Moines. Part of Microsoft's multi-billion dollar total Iowa investment since 2009. Planned MW capacity not confirmed from primary sources; 444 MW figure removed as unsupported. Iowa's Sec. 423.3(95) data-center sales-tax exemption applies, but Iowa data-center incentive awards are not publicly disclosed; no Ginger West-specific job count is published.

edged-aurora-il.name: Edged Chicago Campus — Aurora (ORD01)
edged-aurora-il.water_notes: ThermalWorks liquid-to-chip cooling exceeding 200 kW per rack; zero water consumption for cooling; saves 277M+ gallons annually vs conventional data centers
edged-aurora-il.source: Edged US Expands Chicagoland Campus with Second AI Data Center Groundbreaking
edged-aurora-il.notes: Address: 2835 Bilter Rd, Aurora IL (DuPage County). Total campus planned at 96 MW across three buildings. Explicitly purpose-built for high-density AI workloads. Coordinates approximate for Bilter Rd area of north Aurora; address confirmed in operator press release. A confirmed capex figure of ~$300M covers the first building (ORD01-1) only, not the ~96 MW three-building campus; construction-workforce figures (~2,000 full campus) are projections. No Illinois DCEO data-center exemption certification was found for Edged.

lambda-chicago-edgeconnex-il.name: Lambda Chicago EdgeConneX AI Factory
lambda-chicago-edgeconnex-il.source: Lambda/EdgeConneX joint press release - AI Factory in Chicago and Atlanta
lambda-chicago-edgeconnex-il.notes: EdgeConneX is the developer/facility owner; Lambda is the sole tenant in a build-to-suit, single-tenant, purpose-built 23 MW building for Lambda's AI workloads (600+ kW/rack, hybrid liquid-to-chip + air cooling). Distinct from the excluded CoreWeave/Flexential colo tenancy (a shared multi-tenant colo cage) - this is a dedicated purpose-built building. Press releases say 'Chicago' but EdgeConneX's Chicago-area campus is in Elk Grove Village, IL (Cook County); the Lambda building address is unpublished, so coordinates use the Chicago centroid. Ready-for-Service targeted 2026; operational status as of 2026-07-07 unconfirmed (may already be online - revisit).

project-cardinal-yorkville-il.name: Project Cardinal Data Center Campus
project-cardinal-yorkville-il.water_notes: Air-cooled closed-loop system uses ~42,500 gallons/day (Shaw Local, 2026-03-12), revised down from an original 350,000 gpd proposal; "no municipal water will be used for cooling."
project-cardinal-yorkville-il.source: Project Cardinal Data Center Campus — City of Yorkville official permit page
project-cardinal-yorkville-il.notes: Coordinates approximate NW of IL Rt 47 and Galena Rd in Yorkville; exact parcel spans ~1,037 acres. 14 two-story buildings at 17 million sq ft total. No confirmed hyperscale tenant named. Companion project 'Project Steel' (Prologis, 540 acres, 24 buildings) also approved in same Yorkville corridor. First data center operational target: 2029.

aws-wheatfield-in.name: AWS Wheatfield Campus (Project Rise)
aws-wheatfield-in.water_notes: Natural air cooling ~98% of the year; supplemental water cooling on hot days; campus will not connect to public water systems and will fund its own water/wastewater infrastructure.
aws-wheatfield-in.source: Amazon plans nine-building data center campus in Wheatfield, Indiana
aws-wheatfield-in.notes: Codename Project Rise. Nine-building campus on 304 acres of NIPSCO-owned land ~0.5 mi from the R.M. Schahfer Generating Station; part of AWS's $15B Northern Indiana commitment. CAPACITY OMITTED: data-center IT load not disclosed; the 400 MW figure is NIPSCO's new gas peaker plant, not the facility's load. INVESTMENT OMITTED: DCD reports AWS is 'estimating an investment of around $7 billion' - a soft estimate, so no firm investmentUsd is recorded (noted here). ~250 permanent jobs are a projection (in notes, not jobs). AWS commits to restore 425 acres of Kankakee River watershed habitat and provide $25M for Wheatfield Township water access; AWS committed $1.25B to offset NIPSCO ratepayer impacts across the broader buildout. Coordinates are the Wheatfield centroid. Distinct from Project Rainier (New Carlisle) and the Hobart IN campus.

coreweave-digital-crossroads-hammond-in.name: CoreWeave Digital Crossroads
coreweave-digital-crossroads-hammond-in.source: CoreWeave to develop 180MW data center at Digital Crossroads campus in Hammond, Indiana
coreweave-digital-crossroads-hammond-in.notes: 180 MW facility at the Digital Crossroads campus in Hammond, Lake County; city approved June 2025, NIPSCO lease pending, targeted 2027. Coordinates are the Hammond area centroid. UPDATE (2026-07): the City of Hammond announced the CoreWeave / Decennial development agreement EXPIRED June 30, 2026 - required milestones were not met and no extensions were offered; no groundbreaking occurred. The June 2025 city approval, the 10-year real-property and 20-year personal-property tax abatements, and the ~$2B construction / ~$5B equipment figures were all tied to this now-lapsed agreement (never triggered). Status corrected under_construction -> cancelled.

dc-blox-warren-township-marion-county-in.name: DC BLOX Warren Township Data Center
dc-blox-warren-township-marion-county-in.source: DC Blox data center in eastern Indianapolis receives recommendation for approval
dc-blox-warren-township-marion-county-in.notes: Three-building campus, scaled back from an original 28MW-larger plan. Capex breakout: $700-800M construction + $1.3-1.4B in 'servers, networking equipment, and AI hardware' per the developer's own figures. Coordinates are approximate.

meta-jeffersonville-in.name: Meta Jeffersonville Data Center
meta-jeffersonville-in.powered_by: Grid (100% renewable energy matching; LEED Gold certified)
meta-jeffersonville-in.water_notes: Liquid-cooled hardware for AI workloads; community concern over potential use of up to 5 million gallons/day
meta-jeffersonville-in.notes: River Ridge Commerce Center, Jeffersonville IN (Clark County, across Ohio River from Louisville KY). ~700,000 sq ft; AI-native design with liquid cooling from the start. Coordinates are approximate River Ridge Commerce Center area.

meta-lebanon-in.name: Meta Lebanon (Project Domino)
meta-lebanon-in.powered_by: Grid (100% renewable matching; 400+ MW new Indiana clean energy projects backed by Meta)
meta-lebanon-in.water_notes: Meta pledged 100% water restoration; 200 million gallons/year returned to Upper Wabash River Basin via Arable irrigation partnership with local farmers for 10 years
meta-lebanon-in.source: Meta's New Data Center in Lebanon, Indiana Marks a Milestone AI Investment
meta-lebanon-in.notes: LEAP Innovation and Research District, Lebanon IN (Boone County, ~30 mi NW of Indianapolis). 1,500 acres, 4 million sq ft total; 13 buildings. Among Meta's largest single infrastructure investments. Coordinates are approximate LEAP District area north of Lebanon.

microsoft-laporte-in.name: Microsoft La Porte Data Center
microsoft-laporte-in.source: Gov. Holcomb announces plans for new $1B Microsoft Data Center in Northwest Indiana
microsoft-laporte-in.notes: Radius Industrial Park, La Porte IN (La Porte County, NW Indiana). Initial plan 245,000 sq ft on 489 acres; expanded to 17 buildings with adjacent rezoning sought. First-phase six data centers plus substation. Microsoft stated 'Community-First AI Infrastructure' principles. Coordinates are approximate Radius Industrial Park area. Announcement date corrected from 2024-09 to 2024-06 per IEDC press release dated June 4, 2024.

beale-gardner-johnson-county-ks.name: Beale Infrastructure Gardner Campus
beale-gardner-johnson-county-ks.notes: Near 191st St & S Clare Rd. Up to 16 data halls. Distinct from Beale's existing tracked Project Pilot in De Soto, KS. Coordinates are approximate.

red-wolf-dcd-properties-project-red-wolf.name: Project Red Wolf
red-wolf-dcd-properties-project-red-wolf.source: 600MW data center campus proposed outside Kansas City, Kansas
red-wolf-dcd-properties-project-red-wolf.notes: 400-acre, 6-building campus west of Kansas Speedway (13000 Parallel Parkway). Zoning approval failed a vote and drew a lawsuit; contested, decision pending in 2026.

meta-hyperion-richland-parish-la.name: Meta Hyperion
meta-hyperion-richland-parish-la.water_notes: Sierra Club reporting states ~5 million gallons/day (~2 billion/year). Cooling type not disclosed in primary sources. Meta pledges 100% water restoration by 2030 via a 316-acre restoration project with Resource Environmental Solutions.
meta-hyperion-richland-parish-la.source: Meta to build AI data center in Louisiana — Reuters

rowan-digital-frederick-md.name: Rowan Digital Infrastructure Frederick Campus (Bauxite I)
rowan-digital-frederick-md.water_notes: 440,000 gallons/day cooling water allocated to Rowan's 156-acre parcel per Frederick County records
rowan-digital-frederick-md.source: Rowan secures $1.2bn for Maryland data center campus build-out
rowan-digital-frederick-md.notes: Rowan (Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners + Birch Infrastructure JV) serves as AWS hyperscale host at Quantum Frederick. Three campuses planned on-site total; Bauxite I is Phase 1 at 300MW. 777,150 sq ft total campus footprint. Coordinates approximate for same Quantum Frederick campus area as Aligned record.

project-cannoli-van-buren-township-wayne.name: Project Cannoli
project-cannoli-van-buren-township-wayne.water_notes: Reported to potentially consume up to 3.6 million gallons of water daily.
project-cannoli-van-buren-township-wayne.source: Van Buren Township OKs Google data center substation
project-cannoli-van-buren-township-wayne.notes: Google confirmed evaluating the site. Coordinates are approximate.

google-skyway-pine-island-mn.name: Google Project Skyway (Pine Island)
google-skyway-pine-island-mn.source: Xcel Energy to power new Google data center in Minnesota
google-skyway-pine-island-mn.notes: Google's first Minnesota campus, Pine Island (Goodhue County), powered by Xcel Energy; ~250,000 sq ft initial building for AI applications. Electric Service Agreement pending MPUC approval as of Feb 2026 → proposed. The associated 1,900 MW (1,400 MW wind + 200 MW solar + 300 MW storage) is a new clean-energy build-out, NOT the data center's IT load — DC capacity not disclosed (omitted). Faces a local legal challenge. Coordinates are the Pine Island area centroid.

cloverleaf-troy-mo.name: Cloverleaf Troy Campus
cloverleaf-troy-mo.source: List of upcoming data center projects in Missouri
cloverleaf-troy-mo.notes: 500 MW full-buildout campus near Troy, Lincoln County (near St. Louis); construction from early 2027. Single-tracker source → confidence reported. Coordinates are the Troy area centroid.

lambda-kansas-city-mo.name: Lambda Kansas City AI Supercomputer
lambda-kansas-city-mo.source: AI cloud firm Lambda targets data center deployment in Kansas City, Missouri
lambda-kansas-city-mo.notes: 11155 N. Airworld Dr (former Bank of America campus, ~16.9 acres), Platte County near KCI airport. Launches early 2026 with 24 MW confirmed; >100 MW is a scale-up ceiling (planned figure). Distinct parcels from Google (Project Mica) and Meta's Kansas City sites. Eligible for the Missouri Data Center Sales Tax Exemption (eligibility only — no award amount confirmed; honest-zero). The >$500M figure is a press estimate (notes). Dedicated to a single unnamed AI customer under a multi-year agreement.

digital-realty-charlotte-nc.name: Digital Realty Moores Chapel Data Center Campus
digital-realty-charlotte-nc.water_notes: No cooling type or water volume is disclosed. City Council members raised water-quality concerns at the May 2025 rezoning hearing given proximity to the Catawba River; Charlotte Water is the likely provider.
digital-realty-charlotte-nc.source: Digital Realty files to develop 400MW data center campus in Charlotte, North Carolina
digital-realty-charlotte-nc.notes: 12899 Moores Chapel Road, 12 miles west of downtown Charlotte. Two two-story buildings totaling 3 million sq ft across two phases. Site acquired November 2024 for $160 million. If built, would be largest data center in North Carolina. Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation to receive greenway on site. Coordinates are approximate Moores Chapel Road area.

microsoft-person-county-roxboro-nc.name: Microsoft Person County Mega Park
microsoft-person-county-roxboro-nc.source: Microsoft buys Person County Mega Park for $27 million
microsoft-person-county-roxboro-nc.notes: 1,385-acre Person County Mega Park (Woodsdale township, near Roxboro); ~$26.85M land purchase. Powered by Duke Energy per a Q4-2025 8-K; the campus's MW is in a large-load contract filed under seal (NCUC) — not publicly disclosed (omitted). Coordinates are the Roxboro / Woodsdale area centroid.

meta-los-lunas-ai-nm.name: Meta Los Lunas AI Expansion
meta-los-lunas-ai-nm.utility: Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM)
meta-los-lunas-ai-nm.water_notes: Existing campus is in water-stressed Middle Rio Grande basin; specific cooling type for new AI buildings not disclosed in available sources
meta-los-lunas-ai-nm.source: Meta planning expansion of Los Lunas data center campus in New Mexico
meta-los-lunas-ai-nm.notes: Reported as the first Meta facilities explicitly dedicated to AI/ML workloads. Existing campus is 750 acres. IRBs authorize tax-exempt bond financing for construction materials — the $7.5B per series is the authorized principal ceiling, not a direct cash subsidy. Meta required to invest $350M into expansion by year 10 under agreement.

stargate-project-jupiter-dona-ana-nm.name: Stargate Project Jupiter
stargate-project-jupiter-dona-ana-nm.water_notes: Closed-loop recycling: 20,000 gpd daily average (0.02 MGD), 60,000 gpd maximum, plus a one-time ~10M-gallon initial fill over two years; water via Camino Real Regional Utility Authority. Truthout notes hyperscale closed-loop cooling is not yet proven at a fully operational facility.
stargate-project-jupiter-dona-ana-nm.source: New Mexico's Project Jupiter data center part of larger Stargate AI initiative — El Paso Matters

novva-tahoe-reno-storey-county-nv.name: Novva Tahoe Reno Data Center
novva-tahoe-reno-storey-county-nv.source: Novva Data Centers Announces the Launch of Tahoe Reno Data Center (PR Newswire)
novva-tahoe-reno-storey-county-nv.notes: 300,000 sq ft, 60 MW data center on a 20-acre campus at 1 Astro Way in the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (McCarran / Storey County). Six 10 MW data halls served by an on-campus 100 MW NV Energy substation; water-free direct-to-chip cooling. Coordinates are an approximate TRIC-area geocode (exact parcel point not published).

terawulf-lansing-ny.name: TeraWulf AI Data Center Campus, Lansing
terawulf-lansing-ny.water_notes: TeraWulf proposes closed-loop cooling system; water withdrawal permit application for over 1 million gallons daily from Cayuga Lake submitted to NYSDEC; community contests reliability of closed-loop commitment given LLC structure.
terawulf-lansing-ny.nearest_nuclear_name: R E Ginna Nuclear Power Plant
terawulf-lansing-ny.source: Tompkins County Legislature Urges State to Deny Water Permit for Lansing Data Center
terawulf-lansing-ny.notes: Site is the former Cayuga Power Plant (coal-fired, retired). NYSDEC water permit application for Cayuga Lake withdrawal was originally filed in 2021 for 'unspecified future use.' Permit dates to 1955 without modern monitoring requirements per opposition. TeraWulf also has a separate cryptomining operation at the Susquehanna site in PA (Nautilus).

aws-newton-court-new-albany-oh.name: AWS New Albany (Newton Court)
aws-newton-court-new-albany-oh.source: Licking County Auditor parcel/GIS record (parcel 095-112074-00.000, 2575 Newton Ct — Amazon Data Services Inc, Industrial land-use class 305 'Research/Chemical Labs' = built, 92.7 ac)
aws-newton-court-new-albany-oh.notes: Operational AWS data center on a ~93-acre Amazon Data Services Inc parcel at 2575 Newton Ct, New Albany (~7 km south of the Beech/Miller cluster) — part of Amazon's AWS US-East-2 (Ohio) footprint. Data-center directories label it '2575 Newton' / 'Tower Ultra', built 2024 / fully operational. Licking County Auditor land-use class 305 ('Research/Chemical Labs' = built industrial); owner Amazon Data Services Inc. Data-center directories list numbered Newton addresses (2575/2675/2775/2875/2975) as separate sites, but only one Amazon-owned parcel (095-112074-00.000) exists at 2575 Newton Ct — the numbered addresses are buildings within this single parcel, not distinct sites. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are the Licking County Auditor parcel centroid.

aws-project-cosmos-marysville-oh.name: AWS Project Cosmos
aws-project-cosmos-marysville-oh.powered_by: Grid (city water supply; non-contact cooling with on-site storage)
aws-project-cosmos-marysville-oh.source: AWS gets go-ahead for data center campus in Marysville, Ohio
aws-project-cosmos-marysville-oh.notes: 14684 Industrial Parkway, Marysville OH 43040 (Union County, ~30 mi NW of Columbus). Two-building campus totaling ~500,000 sq ft on 55 acres. Also referenced as 'Project Cosmo' (without trailing 's') in DCD. Jobs updated to 50 per Marysville city FAQ ('at least 50 full-time operational jobs'); original record stated 25 from DCD/Amazon initial filing. Construction start updated to early 2026 per city FAQ; DCD had projected August 2025 which appears delayed. Part of AWS's broader $10B+ Ohio infrastructure commitment. Coordinates are approximate Marysville Innovation Park area.

ark-data-centers-akron-ii-summit-county-.name: Ark Data Centers Akron II (fka Involta)
ark-data-centers-akron-ii-summit-county-.source: Involta / Ark Data Centers — Akron, Ohio
ark-data-centers-akron-ii-summit-county-.notes: 191 E. Miller Ave, Akron, Summit County — same street address as Ark Data Centers Akron I but a physically separate ("4th-generation") building, per the operator's own materials describing "two purpose-built, concurrently maintainable facilities" totaling 52,000+ sq ft. 10,000 sq ft / 300 racks, 1MW utility power with a 1MW N+1 diesel generator, 2N battery UPS. Uptime Institute-certified Tier III — the only Tier certification found across any of the Ark/Involta Ohio sites researched. ENERGY STAR certified 2023. Fiber-ring-connected to the company's Independence, OH facility. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found (one customer testimonial referencing AI describes a tenant's healthcare application, not the operator's own infrastructure marketing).

ark-data-centers-independence-cuyahoga-c.name: Ark Data Centers Independence (fka Involta)
ark-data-centers-independence-cuyahoga-c.source: Involta expands data center in Independence, Ohio
ark-data-centers-independence-cuyahoga-c.notes: 7300 E Pleasant Valley Rd, Independence, Cuyahoga County (Cleveland metro). Rebranded from Involta to Ark Data Centers May 15, 2024 (Carlyle-backed). Fiber-ring-connected to the company's Akron facilities for real-time twinned services, per the City of Independence's own economic development page (independent of operator marketing). A single third-party directory cites 1.5MW capacity, uncorroborated elsewhere — omitted from capacityMw rather than stated as fact. No source supports a Tier rating or 2N+ UPS claim for this specific site (an unrelated "Cleveland" line item on the operator's own rollup page does not reconcile with this facility's known footprint) — no Tier/redundancy field set. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found.

cloverleaf-project-open-sky-piedmont-ok.name: Cloverleaf Project Open Sky
cloverleaf-project-open-sky-piedmont-ok.source: Powered land company Cloverleaf proposing 633-acre data center in Canadian County, Oklahoma
cloverleaf-project-open-sky-piedmont-ok.notes: 630-acre proposed data campus near the Mathewson Substation, NW 248th Street, Piedmont (Canadian/Kingfisher county line) — part of a transmission corridor drawing multiple competing proposals; see beltline-piedmont-kingfisher-county-ok (this same batch), a separate, distinct 321-acre Beltline Energy site nearby — do not conflate despite both being in Piedmont. Closed-loop cooling planned. Cloverleaf recently withdrew from two Wisconsin data center projects after local opposition (context, not this project). Reported as 'over $1 billion taxable investment' (DCD) — read as a tax-abatement eligibility threshold rather than a confirmed capex figure, so not populated as investmentUsd.

google-pryor-ok.name: Google Pryor Data Center Campus (Mayes County Expansion)
google-pryor-ok.powered_by: Grid (Southwest Power Pool) with renewable PPAs
google-pryor-ok.water_notes: Utility records (open-records request) show the Pryor center used more than 1.1 billion gallons Jul 2024–Jun 2025 (≈3.0 MGD, a floor) from the Neosho River via the state-owned MidAmerica Industrial Park; ~253M gallons were discharged back to the river, the remainder lost to evaporative cooling. Google was the park's second-largest water user that year.
google-pryor-ok.source: Google planning another expansion for Pryor data center
google-pryor-ok.notes: Campus operational since 2011; Google's second-largest data center globally per Alphabet CIO Ruth Porat. Four expansions now underway. $5.7B+ invested historically in Oklahoma prior to August 2025 $9B commitment. Expansion capacity and MW not publicly specified. Coordinates are Pryor city center.

stack-hillsboro-or.name: STACK Hillsboro Campus
stack-hillsboro-or.notes: ~75 MW STACK campus in Hillsboro, Washington County, targeted 2029. Single-tracker source → confidence reported. Distinct from STACK's Loudoun, VA campus. Coordinates are the Hillsboro area centroid.

cipher-mclennan-county-tx.name: Cipher McLennan HPC Data Center
cipher-mclennan-county-tx.source: Cipher Digital (Cipher Mining) FY2025 Form 10-K — McLennan Site, central Texas, targeted capacity up to 500 MW, energize 2028; option exercised Feb 2026
cipher-mclennan-county-tx.notes: Cipher's McLennan HPC/AI data center site in central Texas (McLennan County, the Waco area). Targeted capacity up to 500 MW; estimated energization 2028. Cipher entered an option agreement in October 2024 and exercised the option to acquire the special-purpose entity in February 2026. Part of Cipher's ~3.4 GW / 8-site HPC pipeline (Cipher Digital, formerly Cipher Mining). Coordinates approximate (McLennan County / Waco geocode; specific parcel not disclosed).

google-haskell-county-tx.name: Google Haskell County Data Center Campus
google-haskell-county-tx.source: Google data centers totaling $40 billion coming to Texas
google-haskell-county-tx.notes: Two data center buildings at one Haskell County site; treated as a single campus record. Announced Nov 14 2025 as part of Google's $40B Texas investment through 2027 (which also covers Armstrong County and a Wilbarger County/Vernon site); no Haskell-specific investment figure disclosed, so investmentUsd is omitted (the $40B is a Texas-wide aggregate). Data-center IT capacity in MW not publicly disclosed. One building is co-located with the Quantum Clean Energy Project (Intersect Power, acquired by Google March 2026): 640 MW solar PV + 1.3 GWh battery storage, scheduled operational June 2026 - this is energy-project capacity, NOT data-center IT load. Job figures cited in press (1,200 construction / up to 11 permanent) come from the co-located Intersect energy project, not the data center, so they are noted here rather than in jobs. Coordinates are the Haskell city centroid (no parcel-level GPS found).

poolside-project-horizon-pecos-county-tx.name: Poolside Project Horizon AI Campus
poolside-project-horizon-pecos-county-tx.source: Poolside — Announcing Project Horizon: a 2 GW AI campus in Texas
poolside-project-horizon-pecos-county-tx.notes: 2 GW AI training campus on a 568-acre parcel of the Mitchell family's Longfellow Ranch in Pecos County, near Fort Stockton. Coordinate anchored on Fort Stockton (nearest named town in coverage); exact parcel not publicly disclosed. CoreWeave was original anchor tenant (15-year, 250 MW lease, 40,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs) but terminated the lease in late March 2026 after Poolside's Series C funding round failed to close; site reported idle as of mid-2026.

compass-red-oak-tx.name: Red Oak Campus
compass-red-oak-tx.source: Compass Datacenters looks to expand Red Oak campus
compass-red-oak-tx.notes: Second DFW-area Compass site (buildings 3/4). Distinct operator/site from DataBank's separate Red Oak, TX campus (same town, different companies).

qts-eagle-mountain-ut.name: QTS Eagle Mountain Data Center Campus
qts-eagle-mountain-ut.water_notes: A closed-loop system that QTS says does not consume water for cooling once operational — roughly a 600,000-gallon one-time fill per building plus modest domestic use — avoiding an estimated 250–300 million gallons/year versus evaporative cooling.
qts-eagle-mountain-ut.source: QTS begins construction on new datacenter campus in Eagle Mountain — Eagle Mountain City

stack-berry-hill-va.name: Berry Hill / Southern Virginia Megasite
stack-berry-hill-va.source: STACK commits $73.5bn investment into data center campus in Berry Hill, Virginia
stack-berry-hill-va.notes: Performance agreement caps investment at up to $73.5B over 30 years (2,050 jobs); parallel reporting cites a ~$100B project scope. ~2,990 acres of the Southern Virginia Megasite; land deal ~$737.8M.

aws-cosner-technology-campus-massaponax-.name: Cosner Technology Campus
aws-cosner-technology-campus-massaponax-.source: Amazon files for four data center campuses in Spotsylvania and Caroline Counties
aws-cosner-technology-campus-massaponax-.notes: 329 acres in Massaponax, ~1.9M sq ft; one of four AWS Spotsylvania/Caroline campuses (Summit Crossing, Carter's Store, Cosner, Orrock). Spotsylvania case ST23-0031.

culpeper-brandy-station-va.name: Culpeper Acquisitions Brandy Station Campus (denied)
culpeper-brandy-station-va.source: Data Center Watch — Blocked and Delayed Projects Report

emerald-lakes-etheridge-lakes-data-cente.name: Etheridge Lakes Data Center (Great Bridge)
emerald-lakes-etheridge-lakes-data-cente.source: City of Chesapeake Department of Planning, Rezoning Case PLN-REZ-2025-002 (Etheridge Lakes Data Center)
emerald-lakes-etheridge-lakes-data-cente.notes: 22.6-acre parcel on west side of Centerville Turnpike, south of Etheridge Manor Boulevard, Great Bridge area of Chesapeake. Developer Doug Fuller (Emerald Lakes Estates) sought rezoning from agricultural to light industrial; proposed 350,000 sq ft, 35 ft tall, 24/7 staffed facility. City Council denied the rezoning request unanimously. Separately, in July 2026 the Chesapeake Planning Commission recommended a citywide data-center zoning ordinance/policy (conditional use in industrial districts + Fentress Airfield Overlay only) — this is a POLICY change, not a site-specific candidate, and is not included here. No other active Chesapeake DC site rezoning was found this session. Coordinates are approximate (Centerville Turnpike/Great Bridge area); exact parcel not geocoded from GIS this session. Chesapeake City Council denied the rezoning 7-0 on 2025-06-17 (Planning Commission had recommended denial 6-1). Recorded as a cancelled proposal.

gigaland-data-centers-remington-fauquier.name: Gigaland Data Centers
gigaland-data-centers-remington-fauquier.source: Fauquier County planning staff project database (maintained record of application status)
gigaland-data-centers-remington-fauquier.notes: HONEST INTAKE: application on hold, county awaiting additional information from applicant — recorded as status=proposed with the hold explicitly noted. Fauquier planning-database roundup; Planning Commission reportedly recommended denial mid-2025 — treat status as contested/early.

iron-mountain-white-oak-henrico-va.name: Iron Mountain White Oak Technology Park Campus
iron-mountain-white-oak-henrico-va.source: Iron Mountain acquires 66 acres outside Richmond for 200MW data center campus
iron-mountain-white-oak-henrico-va.notes: 6110 Technology Creek Drive, Henrico County (Richmond metro area). White Oak Technology Park has fiber connections and subsea cables to three continents. Henrico County passed stricter data center requirements June 2025, including 500-foot tree buffer near residential. investmentUsd is stated as 'more than $1 billion' — treated as floor.

microsoft-boydton-bn-campus-mecklenburg-.name: Microsoft Boydton Campus (BN / Azure East US)
microsoft-boydton-bn-campus-mecklenburg-.notes: This is the PARENT Microsoft Boydton campus — one of Microsoft's oldest and largest US data center campuses, hosting the Azure 'East US' region, first announced 2010 (~$499M initial investment) and expanded repeatedly through 2011/2013/2014/2015/2019 (cumulative >$2B investment). Distinct from the already-tracked microsoft-skipwith-road-campus-mecklenburg-va (a separate 2022 six-building permit). Located east of Highway 92 / west of Highway 608 (Ridge Road); addresses cited across sources include 101 Herbert Drive and 925 Ridge Rd, Boydton VA — sources differ on whether these are the same 175-

prince-william-digital-gateway-va.name: Prince William Digital Gateway
prince-william-digital-gateway-va.source: Digital Gateway data center project dies after final developer withdraws appeal
prince-william-digital-gateway-va.notes: Would have been largest data center campus in the world at over 22 million sq ft across approximately 2,000-2,100 acres (per WTOP). Cancellation is landmark precedent on Virginia public-notice requirements. Coordinates are approximate for Pageland Lane corridor.

google-project-peanut-chester-va.name: Project Peanut
google-project-peanut-chester-va.source: Google data centers: Chesterfield's Peanut, Skye, Loch
google-project-peanut-chester-va.notes: Part of Google's 3-campus $9B Chesterfield County trio, alongside Project Skye and Project Loch. Distinct from a separately tracked Google Midlothian, VA proposed record.

aws-summit-crossing-tech-campus-spotsylv.name: Summit Crossing Tech Campus
aws-summit-crossing-tech-campus-spotsylv.source: Data Center Frontier — Amazon plans major data center expansion in Spotsylvania County (Summit Crossing: 231 ac, 2.1M sq ft)
aws-summit-crossing-tech-campus-spotsylv.notes: One of Amazon Web Services' four Spotsylvania/Caroline data center campuses (Summit Crossing, Carter's Store, Cosner [tracked as aws-cosner-technology-campus-massaponax-va, ST23-0031], Orrock [tracked as aws-mattermeade-caroline-va]). ~231 acres, up to ~2.1M sq ft of data center buildings (Phase 1 max ~900k sq ft). Located on the south side of Summit Crossing Road, ~0.5 mi west of the Spotsylvania/Caroline county line; borders the Carter's Store campus. Amazon Data Services filed June 2023 to rezone from Rural (RU) to Industrial-1 (I-1); Board of Supervisors approved the four AWS rezonings in a 5-2 vote in October 2023 (Spotsylvania "ST23" case series). Reported under construction / buildings going up per The Fredericksburg Advance (2026). Coordinates approximate (Summit Crossing Road geocode; parcels not GIS-confirmed this pass).

microsoft-east-wenatchee-wa.name: Microsoft East Wenatchee Data Center
microsoft-east-wenatchee-wa.source: New Douglas County Microsoft data center launches — Urban Industrial Way, 340.22 acres, $409M first-building permit, grand opening Dec 2022
microsoft-east-wenatchee-wa.notes: Microsoft Azure data center campus on Urban Industrial Way near Pangborn Memorial Airport, East Wenatchee, Douglas County — first building operational (grand opening Dec 2022), additional buildings under construction, on ~340 acres. Under a Douglas County PUD Schedule 4 power-delivery agreement, Microsoft is contracted for up to 180 MW at full build-out (KPQ, citing the PUD agreement); the first building's permit was valued at $409M (Wenatchee World). DISTINCT from Microsoft's tracked Malaga campus, which is across the Columbia River in Chelan County (served by Chelan County PUD). Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the Urban Industrial Way corridor; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

cassville-grant-county-wi.name: Cassville Data Center Campus (Undisclosed Developer)
cassville-grant-county-wi.developer: Undisclosed (major tech company, NDA not signed)
cassville-grant-county-wi.source: Another $1 billion Wisconsin data center eyed in Grant County town of Cassville
cassville-grant-county-wi.notes: Coordinates are Cassville city centroid; proposed site was ~400-500 acres in the town of Cassville. Grant County ED director confirmed company 'people will recognize' but declined to name it. Energy requirement estimated at 400-500 MW (per Wisconsin Watch, citing economic development director estimate). Investment range $1B-$2B; investmentUsd represents the floor. Town vote was April 16, 2026: 44-0 to ban data centers (ordinance lasts up to two years). Developer went silent post-vote and was reportedly considering Indiana and North Dakota sites.
